chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from more than one person, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever worships Allah with imagination (al-tahammum/al-tawhum) has disbelieved. Whoever worships the Name without understanding the Meaning has disbelieved. Whoever worships both the Name and the Meaning has associated partners with Allah. Whoever worships the Meaning by applying the Names to Him with the attributes with which He described Himself, whose heart is attached to it and whose tongue utters it in his private and public states, they are the followers of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). And in another hadith: 'These are the true believers.'

key_terms.أَشْرَكَ: He associated partners (shirk), specifically in the context of confusing the signifier with the signified.
key_terms.الاسْم: The Name, referring to the verbal designation or label used for Allah.
key_terms.الْتِهَامٍ: Imagination or conceptualization (often read as al-tawhum or al-tahammum), referring to worshipping based on mental constructs rather than divine reality.
key_terms.الْمَعْنَى: The Meaning or Reality, referring to the actual divine essence and attributes behind the name.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between worshipping Allah's Name, His Meaning, and both together in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to delineate the precise boundaries of Tawhid by distinguishing between the Divine Name (al-Ism), the Reality (al-Ma'na), and their attributes. It identifies the Ahl al-Bayt as the true believers who worship the Divine Reality while correctly applying the specific attributes Allah has revealed for Himself, avoiding both the error of mere verbalism and the mistake of conflating the Name with the Essence. This framework underscores the Shia emphasis on aligning one's internal conviction and external declaration with the self-revealed attributes of Allah.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 12. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan alSaffar said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Isa ibn `Ubayd, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, on the authority of `Ali ibn Ri’ab, on the authority of more than one person that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

Whoever serves Allah with his imagination, disbelieves (in Allah). Whoever serves His name without (understanding) the meaning, disbelieves in Allah. Whoever serves both His name and its meaning, has given a partner to Allah. Whoever serves Allah by means of the meanings of the Names of Allah has attributed Himself with, has faith in Allah, which his tongue utters in private and in public. Such are the followers of the Commander of the Faithful. In another version, the last sentence of the tradition is: “These are the true Believes.”
